title: Sales held steady. Profit fell 31%. Find out why by noon.

brief.headline: Sales held steady. Profit fell 31%. Find out why by noon.
brief.story: Kettle & Co runs 14 chai and snack outlets across Bangalore: dine-in, takeaway, and delivery through Swiggy and Zomato. September revenue came in flat against August. Profit didn't. The CEO is meeting investors this afternoon and wants one clear answer for what went wrong, backed by the numbers.

evidence.title: Profit & loss statement
evidence.teaser: Every cost line, August vs September

body.text: Selling & distribution includes marketing spend and delivery-platform commissions.
Platform commission: about 20% of order value after offers. Every delivery order is packed in sealed cups, lids, a sleeve and a bag.

evidence.title: Menu & ticket size
evidence.teaser: Units sold of top items, average bill

body.text: “Rained all week so I just ordered on Swiggy. ₹75 off on Kettle the whole month, can't complain.”
“HSR outlet was half empty on a Sunday morning. Unusual.”
“Indiranagar is cramped. Hard to find a seat.”
“Cups arrive sealed and hot. Better packaging than other chai places.”

causes.label: Milk and raw material prices went up
causes.feedback: Supplier rates per litre and per kg didn't move. Sugar rose ₹1/kg, which is nothing.

causes.label: Theft or leakage at one outlet
causes.feedback: Every one of the 14 outlets lost about 4 margin points. This isn't one bad store.

causes.label: A new competitor took customers away
causes.feedback: Revenue was flat, so customers didn't leave. Something about how they bought changed.

causes.label: Customers moved to delivery, which costs more to serve
Rent went up
causes.feedback: Rent rose ₹0.5L. Profit fell ₹3.9L. Rent is part of the story, not the cause.

causes.label: Wastage from the new cold coffee
causes.feedback: Wastage went from 2.1% to 2.3%, worth about ₹8,000. Far too small.

causes.label: Overstaffing and overtime
causes.feedback: Headcount and payroll were flat. Overtime actually dropped.

causes.label: Heavy discounting on the dine-in menu
causes.feedback: The average bill barely moved and dine-in prices weren't cut.

causes.label: Higher payment gateway and UPI fees
causes.feedback: "Other costs", where gateway fees sit, rose only ₹0.2L.

causes.label: Smaller average order value
causes.feedback: The average bill fell from ₹186 to ₹184. That's under ₹1L of impact.

causes.label: Packaging supplier is overcharging
causes.feedback: The price per cup didn't change. Kettle is buying more packaging, not paying more for each piece.

bonus.question: What should the CEO do first?
options: Renegotiate the milk contract to bring the per-litre rate down.
Price the delivery menu above the counter menu and stop funding platform discounts.
Close the two lowest-margin outlets, Electronic City and Yelahanka.
Cut headcount to bring staff costs in line with the lower profit.
bonus.explanation: The leak is the cost of each delivery sale: commission plus packaging. Pricing delivery 15-20% above the counter and dropping the ₹75-off offer fixes the margin without losing customers. Milk rates and staffing never moved, and every outlet fell by the same amount, so closing stores fixes nothing.

why: Revenue stayed the same, but ₹12.2L of it moved from the counter to Swiggy and Zomato, probably pushed by a month-long ₹75-off offer and a rainy September.

Delivery is a worse sale. At about 20% commission, the extra ₹12.8L of delivery revenue cost **₹2.5L in commissions**, which is exactly the jump in selling & distribution. Every delivery order also needs a sealed cup, lid, sleeve and bag, which is the **₹1.3L packaging increase** hiding inside food costs. That accounts for ₹3.8L of the ₹3.9L drop.
fastest_path: Open the P&L. Selling & distribution (+₹2.5L) is the biggest mover, and it holds platform commissions.
Open sales by channel. Delivery went from 22% to 37% of sales. 20% of the extra ₹12.8L is ₹2.5L. Case closed.
explanation.traps: Food costs went up, which points at milk prices, but supplier rates were flat. Rent went up, but only by ₹0.5L. The new cold coffee looks suspicious, but the wastage is tiny.
explanation.fix: Price the delivery menu 15-20% above the counter menu, stop funding the platform discount, and push repeat delivery customers to a direct WhatsApp order line.
